Ledger Row

List keyed facts as rows, each with its chips, one line of evidence and its source, and show by fidelity which rows are proven, which are a reading, and which disagree with another record.

States

Anatomy

#PartType roleToken (CSS variable)
1LedgerThe frame: surface, hairline border, rows separated by hairlinessurface, border
2KeyMono, sentence case, at the label step; a left column from a 38rem container, above the body below ittext-secondary
3Chips28 Chip row: owner and status in words; colour by its one meaningplain, cyan, green, gold, red
4BodyOne or two sentences of evidencetext
5Source32 Evidence ref: timestamp, file or command the row rests ondimmed
6Fidelity37 classes on the row: grain for grade D or not scored (no motion), moire plus a magenta tint where two records disagreemagenta, magenta-bg

Usage

Use it when

  • Facts that share a shape (commitments, forecasts, readings) and each need an owner, a status and a source.
  • A short skim table at the top of a page, one row a section, each linking to its fold.

Do not use it when

  • Do not render a grade D forecast as a bar; it is a grain row with n = k in its body.
  • Do not use green for a reading or red for a parked idea. Colour has one meaning across the kit (arc weld spec 4.3): red a failed check, gold a limit, green proven, cyan an action or focus, plain (steel) unknown, magenta a paradox.
  • Do not use it for a comparison across many columns; that is a table.

Data it reads

FieldTypeRequiredNote
rows[]{key, chips[], body, ref, state}yesstate is plain, grain or moire; chips[] are {label, tone}.

Access

  • Rows are plain block elements in source order; the key comes first, so a screen reader reads key, chips, body, source.
  • Fidelity never hides text: grain lowers weight and adds texture at full opacity; moire adds a tint and keeps the chip text.
  • The grid uses minmax(0, 1fr) and rem sizes, so large text wraps inside the row.
